_note: B-32. Group membership write levers (PowerShell, mock tenant). Mock only; no real Entra group is changed. Registered risk class is R2, the stricter of the two; the call's own class (R2 data access, R1 distribution) is reported in the dry-run data from the group's redlineAccessClass attribute.

levers.name: group.add-member
levers.description: Mock of adding one user to a group of the client. Refuses a role-assignable or client-privileged group (W-IDM-07). R2 when the group grants data access, R1 for distribution only (shown in the dry-run data).

upn.description: userPrincipalName of one user of this client

group_id.description: Object id of one group of this client

impact.L1: One person gets the access that group carries, on day one or after a move, without waiting; the wrong group would show them files or mail they should not see.
impact.L2: The practice's records, shares and mailing lists stay limited to the people who need them; an over-broad group is a data exposure for the client.
impact.L3: Access requests become one approved, audited, reversible change; admin-capable groups are refused outright, so no automated path can grant admin rights.
impact.L4: Least privilege applied the same way at every client, so one weak group habit at one office does not become a way into the others.

levers.name: group.remove-member
levers.description: Mock of removing one user from a group of the client; the undo of group.add-member. Refuses a role-assignable or client-privileged group (W-IDM-07).

upn.description: userPrincipalName of one user of this client

group_id.description: Object id of one group of this client

impact.L1: One person loses the access that group carried, for example after a move to another role; removing the wrong person can lock them out of work files.
impact.L2: Access follows the person's current job, so old access to records does not linger after a move.
impact.L3: Removals are as controlled as additions: approved, audited, and reversible with the other lever.
impact.L4: Stale access is a common route for misuse; routine, consistent clean-up lowers it across all clients.
